plugins.name: strategy-frameworks
plugins.description: Strategic Thinking Agent — meta-router for 47 business strategy frameworks (Porter Five Forces/Value Chain/Generic Strategies, Drucker MBO/5Q, BSC, Blue Ocean, Wardley Mapping, BCG Matrix, BMC, Lean Startup, OKR, Disruptive Innovation, Scenario Planning, Real Options, Game Theory, and more). Invoke /think to auto-select optimal frameworks.

skills.name: ansoff-matrix
skills.description: Ansoff Growth Matrix — four strategic growth options: Market Penetration, Product Development, Market Development, Diversification. Essential for growth strategy decisions with risk assessment.
headings: Ansoff Growth Matrix — Choose the Right Growth Path

skills.name: bcg-matrix
skills.description: BCG Growth-Share Matrix — portfolio management framework for allocating resources across business units. Classify units as Stars, Cash Cows, Dogs, or Question Marks based on market growth and relative market share.
headings: BCG Growth-Share Matrix — Manage Your Portfolio of Businesses
Quadrant 1: Stars (스타) — High Growth, High Share
Quadrant 2: Cash Cows (자금젖소) — Low Growth, High Share
Quadrant 3: Question Marks (물음표) — High Growth, Low Share
Quadrant 4: Dogs (개) — Low Growth, Low Share
Limitations and Modern Updates (한계점 및 현대적 보완)

skills.name: blue-ocean
skills.description: Blue Ocean Strategy (Kim & Mauborgne) — create uncontested market space instead of competing in bloody red oceans. Includes Blue Ocean Shift (2017) process, Buyer Utility Map, and Pioneer-Migrator-Settler Map.
headings: Blue Ocean Strategy — Make the Competition Irrelevant
Step 5: Validate with BOI (Blue Ocean Idea) Index
Step 3: Imagine Where You Could Be
Step 4: Find How to Get There

skills.name: bmc
skills.description: Business Model Canvas (Osterwalder & Pigneur) — visualize, design, and pivot business models using 9 building blocks. Includes Value Proposition Canvas for customer fit analysis.

skills.name: bsc
skills.description: Balanced Scorecard (Kaplan & Norton) — translate strategy into action across 4 perspectives: Financial, Customer, Internal Process, Learning & Growth. Includes Strategy-Focused Organization principles. Use for strategic planning, KPI design, and aligning organization around strategy.
headings: Step 3: Define Objectives, Measures, Targets, Initiatives
Five Principles of a Strategy-Focused Organization
Principle 1: Translate Strategy into Operational Terms
Principle 2: Align the Organization to the Strategy
Principle 3: Make Strategy Everyone's Everyday Job
Principle 4: Make Strategy a Continual Process
Principle 5: Mobilize Change Through Executive Leadership

skills.name: design-thinking
skills.description: Design Thinking (Stanford d.school / IDEO) — human-centered innovation through Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test. Use when building products/services, improving customer experience, or solving ambiguous problems.
headings: Design Thinking — Solve the Right Problem for Real People

skills.name: disruptive-innovation
skills.description: Disruptive Innovation (Clayton Christensen) — predict and respond to market disruption. Understand why great companies fail, how low-end and new-market disruption works, and how incumbents can defend or disrupt themselves.
headings: 1. 🧠 Core Theory: The Innovator's Dilemma (혁신기업의 딜레마)
Why Good Management Leads to Failure
2. 📊 Two Types of Disruption (파괴적 혁신의 두 유형)
Type A: Low-End Disruption (저가 시장 파괴)
4. ✅ Disruption Litmus Test (파괴적 혁신 판별 검증)
Condition 1: Does the entrant target overserved customers or non-consumers? (과잉서비스 고객 또는 비소비자를 대상으로 하는가?)
Condition 2: Does the innovation have a trajectory that will eventually meet mainstream needs? (궤적이 결국 주류 시장의 요구를 충족시킬 수 있는가?)
Condition 3: Is the incumbent's business model unable to respond? (기존 기업의 비즈니스 모델이 대응할 수 없는 구조인가?)
5. 🎯 Jobs to Be Done (JTBD) Integration (해결 과제 이론)

skills.name: drucker
skills.description: Drucker's Management Frameworks (Peter Drucker) — MBO (Management by Objectives), Five Essential Questions, Effective Executive habits, Seven Sources of Innovation. The foundation of modern management. Use for goal-setting, organizational self-assessment, executive effectiveness, and systematic innovation.
headings: Peter Drucker — The Practice of Management
The 8 Key Result Areas (where objectives are needed)
Practice 1: Know Where Your Time Goes
Framework 4: Seven Sources of Innovation (Innovation and Entrepreneurship, 1985)
Key Drucker Quotes as Decision Filters

skills.name: first-principles
skills.description: First Principles Thinking — break problems down to fundamental truths and reason up from there. Use when conventional wisdom is wrong, costs seem fixed, or 'that's how it's always been done' blocks progress.
headings: First Principles Thinking — Reason from the Ground Up
Musk: Applied First Principles at Scale

skills.name: game-theory
skills.description: Game Theory for Business Strategy — analyze competitive interactions, predict rival behavior, and design winning strategies. Prisoner's Dilemma, Nash Equilibrium, commitment devices, and co-opetition.
headings: 🎯 Game Theory for Business Strategy (게임이론 전략 분석)
Mixed Strategy Nash Equilibrium (혼합 전략 균형)
Game Trees and Backward Induction (역진 귀납법)

skills.name: jtbd
skills.description: Jobs to Be Done (Christensen/Ulwick) — understand why customers 'hire' products. Uncover the functional, emotional, and social jobs that drive purchase decisions. The foundation of outcome-driven innovation.

skills.name: kotter
skills.description: Kotter's 8-Step Change Model — lead organizational transformation from urgency to culture. The definitive change management framework with 2014 Accelerate dual-system update.
headings: Why 70% of Change Efforts Fail — 8 Common Errors
🔭 Step 3: Form Strategic Vision (전략적 비전 수립)
🙋 Step 4: Enlist Volunteer Army (자발적 참여 유도)
🔓 Step 5: Enable Action by Removing Barriers (장애물 제거)
🏆 Step 6: Generate Short-term Wins (단기 성과 창출)
Kotter's Accelerate (2014 Update): Dual Operating System

skills.name: lean-startup
skills.description: Lean Startup (Eric Ries) — Build-Measure-Learn loop for rapid validated learning. MVP, pivot-or-persevere decisions, innovation accounting. Reduce waste by testing assumptions before building.
headings: CRITICAL: Plan in REVERSE Order (계획은 역순으로!)
Vanity Metrics vs Actionable Metrics (허영 지표 vs 실행 지표)

skills.name: marketing-mix
skills.description: Marketing Mix 4P/7P Framework (McCarthy/Booms & Bitner) — Product, Price, Place, Promotion + People, Process, Physical Evidence for services. The tactical execution layer of marketing strategy.

skills.name: mckinsey-7s
skills.description: McKinsey 7S Framework — diagnose organizational alignment across 7 interdependent elements: Strategy, Structure, Systems, Shared Values, Style, Staff, Skills. Essential for change management and M&A integration.
headings: Hard S's (하드 요소) — Tangible, Easier to Change
Soft S's (소프트 요소) — Intangible, Harder to Change
Which S's to Change — and in What Order

skills.name: okr
skills.description: OKR (Objectives and Key Results) — goal-setting framework from Intel/Google. Align organization through ambitious objectives with measurable key results. Includes CFR (Conversations, Feedback, Recognition) for continuous performance management.
headings: 📊 Key Result 작성 규칙 (핵심 결과 작성법)
📜 OKR의 역사: Andy Grove → John Doerr → Google

skills.name: ooda
skills.description: OODA Loop — John Boyd's rapid decision-making framework. Observe-Orient-Decide-Act. Use for fast-changing situations, competitive response, crisis management, or when the user needs to outpace competitors.

skills.name: porter
skills.description: Porter's Frameworks (Michael Porter) — Five Forces for industry analysis, Value Chain for competitive advantage, Generic Strategies for positioning, Diamond Model for national advantage. The gold standard of competitive strategy analysis.
headings: Porter's Strategic Frameworks — Understand Competitive Forces
Force 2: Threat of New Entrants (신규 진입 위협)
Force 3: Bargaining Power of Suppliers (공급자 교섭력)
Force 4: Bargaining Power of Buyers (구매자 교섭력)
Porter's 2008 HBR Update: The Sixth Force

skills.name: pyramid-principle
skills.description: Pyramid Principle (Barbara Minto, McKinsey) — structure thinking and communication top-down. Answer first, then support with logically grouped arguments. The gold standard of executive communication.
headings: 4. Two Ways to Build a Pyramid (피라미드 구축 방법)
7. Inductive vs Deductive Reasoning (귀납 vs 연역)

skills.name: rbv
skills.description: Resource-Based View (Barney/Wernerfelt) — build competitive advantage from unique internal resources and capabilities. VRIO framework for identifying sustainable advantages. Complements Porter's outside-in with inside-out perspective.
headings: 3.2 Three Reasons for Inimitability (모방 불가의 3가지 원인)
7. RBV vs Porter: Inside-Out vs Outside-In (비교)

skills.name: real-options
skills.description: Real Options Analysis — apply options thinking to strategic investments under uncertainty. Value the right (not obligation) to expand, defer, abandon, or switch. Turns uncertainty from threat into opportunity.
headings: 1. Why NPV Alone Fails — The "Now or Never" Fallacy (전통 NPV의 한계)
5. When to Use Real Options vs. Traditional NPV (판단 기준)

skills.name: scenario-planning
skills.description: Scenario Planning (Shell/Schwartz method) — strategic foresight through multiple plausible futures. Build robust strategies that work across different scenarios instead of betting on one prediction.
headings: Shell/Schwartz Method — Strategic Foresight Through Multiple Plausible Futures
Why Prediction Fails and Scenario Planning Works (왜 예측은 실패하고 시나리오 플래닝은 성공하는가)
The Scenario Planning Process (시나리오 플래닝 프로세스) — 8 Steps
Step 1: Identify the Focal Question (핵심 질문 정의)
Step 3: Rank by Uncertainty and Impact (불확실성 × 영향력 평가)
Step 4: Select 2 Critical Uncertainties → 2x2 Scenario Matrix (2x2 시나리오 매트릭스)
Step 5: Develop 4 Scenario Narratives (4개 시나리오 서사 개발)
Step 6: Identify Signposts and Early Warning Signals (신호 및 조기경보 지표)
Step 7: Test Strategies Against All 4 Scenarios — Wind Tunneling (전략 풍동 테스트)
Step 8: Develop Robust Strategy + Contingency Triggers (강건한 전략 + 비상 트리거)
Wind Tunneling in Detail (풍동 테스트 상세)

skills.name: stp
skills.description: STP Marketing Framework — Segmentation, Targeting, Positioning. The foundation of marketing strategy: divide the market, choose your target, position your offering. Essential before any marketing mix (4P) decision.
headings: 3.3 Points of Parity vs Points of Difference

skills.name: swot-pestel
skills.description: SWOT + PESTEL Analysis — internal strengths/weaknesses and external opportunities/threats combined with macro-environment scanning (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, Legal). Foundation of strategic planning.
headings: SWOT + PESTEL Analysis — Strategic Environment Scanning

skills.name: systems-thinking
skills.description: Systems Thinking (Peter Senge) — understand complex systems through feedback loops, mental models, and leverage points. Use when problems keep recurring, fixes backfire, or the whole is behaving differently than expected from its parts.
headings: Systems Thinking — See the Forest AND the Trees
Step 6: Identify Leverage Points (Meadows' 12, most to least powerful)

skills.name: think
skills.description: Strategic Thinking Agent — automatically selects the best framework(s) from 47 tools (TOC/TRIZ/Wardley/OODA/Systems Thinking/Blue Ocean/Design Thinking/First Principles/Porter/Drucker/BSC + 17 MBA frameworks) to solve any business problem. Just describe your problem.
headings: Strategic Thinking Agent — 47 Tools, One Entry Point

skills.name: wardley
skills.description: Wardley Mapping — visualize value chains by evolution stage to make better strategic decisions. Use when the user needs to analyze competitive positioning, build-vs-buy decisions, or identify strategic moves.
